senses.sense_definition: The quality of being likely to change suddenly and unexpectedly, especially for the worse.

examples.text: The political <w>volatility</w> in the region makes investors very nervous about the future.
Market <w>volatility</w> can lead to significant losses for those who are not prepared.

senses.sense_definition: A measure of how much the price of a financial asset is expected to change over a period of time.

examples.text: Investors often use <w>volatility</w> as a key indicator when assessing the risk of a stock.
The <w>volatility</w> of the cryptocurrency market is much higher than that of traditional government bonds.

senses.sense_definition: The tendency of a substance to evaporate quickly at normal temperatures.

examples.text: The high <w>volatility</w> of gasoline means it must be stored in tightly sealed containers.
Scientists measured the <w>volatility</w> of the chemical to determine how safely it could be handled.

senses.sense_definition: The characteristic of computer memory that causes it to lose stored data when the power is turned off.

examples.text: Because of the <w>volatility</w> of RAM, all unsaved work is lost when the computer shuts down.
Engineers must account for memory <w>volatility</w> when designing systems that require constant data retention.

senses.sense_definition: The general state of being easily changed or prone to rapid, extreme shifts.

examples.text: The <w>volatility</w> of his temper made it difficult for his colleagues to work with him.
She was concerned about the <w>volatility</w> of the situation during the protest.

senses.sense_definition: The ability to fly or move through the air.

examples.text: The <w>volatility</w> of the small bird allowed it to escape the predator quickly.
Researchers studied the <w>volatility</w> of various insect species to understand their migration patterns.

traits.comment: This sense is rarely used in modern English.
